newsitem.title: GERMANY: France will not hinder Europe integration - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: France will not hinder Europe integration - Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Tuesday he did not think France's new left-wing government would hold back plans for European integration after it proposed delaying a key plank of monetary union.

"France's behaviour will in no way mean we are going to be hamstrung," Kinkel told reporters at a reception in Bonn. He was responding to France's call to delay a planned stability pact intended to underpin European monetary union (EMU).
Germany media cautioned that France's proposed delay in the pact seriously jeopardised plans to launch Europe's single currency, the euro.

The pact, proposed by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel to quell Germans' fears over swapping their beloved deutschmark for a possibly weaker currency, is due for ratification at next week's European Union summit in Amsterdam.

But at a meeting of EU finance ministers in Luxembourg on Monday, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said Paris needed time to study the stability pact, designed to enforce fiscal restraint among EMU member states.

German government sources said there was no strict link between the Amsterdam summit and the stability pact. Kinkel said much would be expected of German-French cooperation in the next few weeks -- cooperation which, he said, was of central importance to Europe.
